conventions: Also tag 'duolingo' if the sentence comes from Duolingo.
Never put the sound tag in Front too: the templates already play Audio with the Latin side.
Set audio.text to the plain Latin text so speech is never generated from HTML.
Voice is eSpeak on purpose: Google's 'la' is not Latin.

fields.Learnable: Spanish word or sentence as the user encountered it, with correct spelling, accents and punctuation; nouns with article. Alternative accepted answers go AFTER the main one inside alt 1|alt 2, never with ';'. The multiple-choice cards show only the main answer. Only near-identical variants are alts (see conventions); anything with a different word or pronunciation gets its own note.
fields.Definition: natural English translation; if several are natural, list them separated by ' / '
fields.Choices: REQUIRED (the multiple-choice cards are blank without it): exactly 5 wrong Spanish options separated by ' | ', each shaped like the answer (same length and structure). Words: look-alikes or sound-alikes and related-but-different words (atardecer -> el amanecer | la madrugada | el mediodía). Sentences: near-misses that change one thing: wrong conjugation or person, ser/estar, wrong preposition or article gender, a swapped content word (season, time of day, activity). NEVER a decoy that is also a correct answer for the English prompt: no tú/usted/ustedes swaps when the English 'you' is ambiguous, no valid synonyms, no regional variants, nothing listed in the alt span. No '|' inside an option.
fields.Extra: short context shown on the front. Required when the English prompt has several distinct Spanish answers split into separate notes, so the prompt says which one is wanted: 'informal' / 'formal' / 'Mexico' (e.g. tu piscina = informal, su piscina = formal, tu alberca = Mexico, informal). Otherwise empty.
fields.Extra 2: optional note shown on the back: register notes, literal meaning, all accepted variants spelled out (standard vs informal), sibling notes ('Formal: su piscina (own card)'), where it was heard; e.g. 'From Duolingo'

conventions: Words and sentences both use this note type. Each note makes 4 cards: translation and listening, each as multiple choice and as type-in. The user dropped tapping cards on 2026-09-29 (little value, trivial for one-word items).
Always fill Choices, also when tidying phone-added notes (they arrive with Choices empty), and include the decoys in the dry run so the user can review them.
Leave Mems empty. Attributes is optional: 'noun' / 'verb' to tell apart pairs like el atardecer / atardecer.
If the user says where the word or sentence came from, put it in Extra 2.
With alternatives, the main (non-alt) answer is the most standard one, and audio.text is that main answer only.
When the user's phrasing is informal or nonstandard, keep it as an alt and mark it in Extra 2 rather than dropping it.

Notes typed on the phone have only the main answer in Learnable and no audio. Alternatives may be written as plain text in Extra 2 (e.g. 'also: X | informal: Y') or, by mistake, in Choices (e.g. 'X; Y'). When tidying, move them into X|Y after the main answer (or into separate notes, per the split rule), rewrite Extra 2 as a labelled note (Standard: ... / Very informal: ...), and replace Choices with real decoys.

Split rule (user, 2026-09-30): an alternative that uses a different word or sounds clearly different (tú vs usted conjugation, su vs tu, piscina vs alberca) is NOT an alt: it becomes its own note with its own audio, and each sibling gets a front Extra hint (informal / formal / Mexico) so the English prompt is unambiguous. Only near-identical variants stay as alts: dropped subject pronoun (yo/él/ellos), ellos/ellas, gender endings (amigo/amiga, perezoso/perezosa), punctuation.

fields.Word: Spanish word, nouns with article (la cumbre); expressions as-is
fields.WordType: one of N, V, Adj, Adv, Expr, Prep, Pron, Conj, Num
fields.Gender: m, f or m/f for nouns; empty otherwise

conventions: Leave Word_suffix, Word_hint, Meaning_suffix, Meaning_hint empty.
Tag Spanish::Duolingo::<nn>_<Topic> if the user names a matching topic, otherwise Spanish::Added.

fields.Text: (part of speech) definition. Example sentence with the word as {{c1::word}}; an optional IPA transcription may follow the word inside the cloze, e.g. {{c1::virile /ˈvɪr.əl/}}

conventions: Audio speaks only the cloze word: use add_audio with cloze_only=true (IPA and hints are dropped).
For new notes via add_notes, set audio.text to the plain cloze word without transcription.

Google en-US (and en-CA) mispronounces some rare words, e.g. chimerical; en-GB got it right. If the user reports a wrong pronunciation, they clear Back Extra in Anki and you re-voice that one note with en-GB; if en-GB is wrong too, try macos:Samantha (used for kvetch).
